rules.rule_name: Structured Output and JSON Schema Enforcement
rules.explanation: Relying on unstructured free-form text responses from LLMs makes downstream software parsing brittle and prone to runtime errors.
rules.do: Enforce strict output formats using JSON Mode, Function Calling, or Pydantic schema validation for predictable integration.
rules.dont: Do not parse free-text LLM completions using raw regular expressions without fallback error handling.

rules.rule_name: Systemic Prompt Engineering and System Instructions
rules.explanation: Vague user-level prompts lead to inconsistent model outputs, hallucinations, and security vulnerabilities.
rules.do: Separate system instructions, domain context, constraints, and user input clearly using structured delimiters and system roles.
rules.dont: Do not concatenate untrusted user text directly into system instructions without clear isolation barriers.

rules.explanation: Full fine-tuning of large models requires excessive GPU memory and compute. Parameter-efficient techniques achieve comparable domain performance at a fraction of the cost.
rules.do: Utilize LoRA, QLoRA, or adapter modules when adapting open-weights LLMs to specialized tasks.
rules.dont: Do not perform full parameter retrain on multi-billion parameter models when PEFT adapters suffice.

rules.rule_name: Token Budget and Context Window Management
rules.explanation: Exceeding token limits causes truncation errors, dropped conversation history, and exponentially higher API billing costs.
rules.do: Implement token counting, context sliding windows, or summarization pipelines to manage prompt payloads within model constraints.
rules.dont: Do not pass unchecked long documents directly into context windows without chunking or token counting.
